title: The stUSDS Rate is the Sky Savings Rate plus a utilization-scaled share of the borrow spread, minus a risk deduction
content:
A.4.4.1.3.2 gives the yield formula in full:

`stUSDS Rate = Sky Savings Rate + (SKY Borrow Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) * Utilization - Rfactor * f(Utilization)`

Each term answers a distinct design question. **Anchoring on the Sky Savings Rate** sets the baseline at the depositor's opportunity cost: USDS could simply have earned the Savings Rate with no lending risk and no liquidity lock, so stUSDS must start there and add a premium, otherwise nobody supplies capital.

**Multiplying the spread by Utilization** means lenders are paid on capital actually working. Idle deposits earn only the Savings Rate; a fully utilized pool passes through the entire spread. This is the standard variable-rate lending curve, and it makes the supply side self-balancing — as utilization rises, yield rises, attracting deposits that push utilization back down.

**Subtracting `Rfactor * f(Utilization)`** is the unusual term. It withholds an amount that grows with utilization, so the same condition that raises the gross yield also raises the deduction. Whatever `Rfactor` funds — loss absorption or reserve accumulation — it is collected fastest when the pool is most exposed, which is the correct time to be building a buffer rather than distributing everything to lenders.

The net effect is a rate that cannot fall below the Savings Rate benchmark, rises with genuine demand for SKY-backed credit, and automatically tightens its distribution as risk concentrates.
description: `SSR + (SKY Borrow Rate - SKY Borrow Minimum Rate) * Utilization - Rfactor * f(Utilization)` anchors the floor to the savings rate and pays lenders only for capital actually lent.
